newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Lindsey calls U.S. economy strong on balance.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Lindsey calls U.S. economy strong on balance.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Governor Lawrence Lindsey said the U.S. economy appears, on balance, to be a bit strong, adding that the central bank will not curb growth provided inflation remains in check.
Speaking on the U.S. cable television network CNBC, Lindsey said, "I think that on balance, it (the economy) is looking a little bit on the strong side."
However, the Fed governor said the economy is still sending some "mixed signals."
Lindsey said the Fed has no intention of restraining growth when there is no evidence of price pressures.
"We don't want, as a matter of policy, to stop a robust, real growth economy that isn't inflationary," he said.
At the same time, Lindsey suggested the central bank does not want to get behind the inflation curve.
"Once you get inflation so that everyone can point to it, and see it ... it might be too late.
"So the flip side is that you want to act before inflation is obvious to everyone," Lindsey added.

As for the data the Fed examines to determine the course of monetary policy, Lindsey noted that the central bank does not focus on any particular indicator and instead watches all measures of growth and inflation.
Lindsey was asked if the upcoming National Association of Purchasing Management's August index or payroll employment for the month would be most crucial.
"While those are both very important pieces of information, I don't think any one piece of data is critical," Lindsey responded, "but we'll be watching the entire picture as it unfolds."
The Fed governor cautioned that the risks in the economy are for possibly some overheating.

"When the economy is expanding this solidly, when we have this level of unemployment ... the greater risks are clearly that we might see some overheating," noted Lindsey. "And besides, it's our job to prevent overheating."
